quick.summary: Why two teams get different numbers, and how one written definition fixes it.
quick.takeaway: Write who counts, what they did, and when.

beats.line: My active users and finance’s active users don’t match. Who is wrong?
Maybe nobody. What does active mean to you?
Finance might count anyone who paid this month. Two metrics, one name.
Isn’t writing it down a lot of fuss for one word?
One word, two numbers, and every meeting starts with an argument. Write it down.
Three parts. Who counts, what they did, and the time window.
Active: anyone who opened a report in the last seven days.

board.text: opened a report, last seven days

beats.line: Share it for review. Finance’s number gets its own name, like paying users.

quiz.question: Two teams report different numbers for active users. What is the most likely cause?
options: One team made a typing mistake
quiz.explanation: The same name often hides different rules about who counts and over what time.

quiz.question: A metric definition only needs a name everyone recognises.
quiz.explanation: It needs who counts, the action that counts and the time window, written down.
